doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

chapter: Joe Rene: Lewis, the Rena band and New Orleans
title: Where Lewis played with the Rena band; Zeb DeMorris's clarinet style
summary: Rene recalls dances where Lewis sat in and the band's regular clarinetist Zeb DeMorris, whose style he disliked.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, we used to play dances. We played dances. If I can remember that. You got something... I got to dig my mind now. Because he just... he didn't regularly say he played with the band. Studies. We used to iron. Yeah. We used to iron, yeah. Let's see if I had something to think about now. Well, we used to play that. Oh, I know he never played at the colony. He'd incorporate all over with us. Because we had a fella. Zeb DeMorris played at the colony at that time.
Was he more your regular kind of player?

Yeah, who? Zeb. Zeb, yeah. He was our regular kind of player. Oh, I know. I know. He used to play... I've never seen him ever play... He used to play cland on the side like that. Really? Yeah. He played a cland on the... Oh, it! Yeah, the style is odd. That's right. He had a cland in there. He had a cland in there. He had a cland in there.
I don't understand. What was he... Was he any good?

Oh, he had a cland in style, but I didn't like it. I didn't like his style. He had some kind of variation he made there. But it looked like to me, it was a little cland off, you know. He didn't have the real homie, you know. See, like George, like George said, but he stood right in homie, right in the key, you know. But all that stuff he made, he stood right there in the key. But once he looked like he was kind of... I never did like it. I used to come up with all the time. I said, okay. I tried to get a real good cland in there.
